narration: GitHub went down again. October seventh. Webhooks, Actions, pull requests.
One tracker counted two hundred fifty seven incidents in twelve months. Forty eight of them major.
So I built snapgit. Git that disappears on purpose.

code:
$ snapgit snap wip/login --ttl 2h
📸 wip/login will disappear in 2h (2026-10-10 20:27Z). Commit fast.

$ snapgit ls
wip/login                      33b0bf5  2h left
caption: Self-destruct timer
narration: Branches get a self destruct timer. When it hits zero, it's gone.

code:
$ snapgit pr open 7d7111d5
Fix login   #7d7111d5
  33b0bf5 fix login
+export const login = () => "ok";
⏳ the fuse is lit: wip/login merges into main in 1m unless you run: snapgit pr reject 7d7111d5
caption: One button: reject
narration: Pull requests have exactly one button. Open one, and a sixty second fuse is lit. You can read every changed line. Or you can reject it.

code:
$ snapgit sweep -r origin
🔀 PR 7d7111d5: nobody rejected it, so wip/login merged into main and was pushed
$ git log --oneline --graph
*   772fef0 Merge wip/login into main
|\  
| * 33b0bf5 fix login
|/  
* a689d11 init
caption: No reject? It merges.
narration: Don't reject it, and it merges. Merge by neglect.
No servers, so there's nothing to take down. snapgit. Link in bio. Hosted on GitHub. We know.
